**A light‑weight weekly “Laundry + Vacuum” routine**

Below is a simple, day‑by‑day schedule that breaks the two chores into short, repeatable blocks.  It follows the **point‑person** idea from [[summaries/session-37_2025-02-11]] and the “keep the existing split” pattern from [[summaries/session-14_2024-06-12]].  The goal is to keep each effort under 15 minutes on any given day, so the work never feels like a big “once‑a‑week” mountain.

| Day | Laundry task (≈ 5‑15 min) | Vacuum task (≈ 5 min) | Quick notes |
|-----|--------------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| **Mon** | **Sort & start** – pull out the week’s dirty clothes, separate whites / colors, toss the first load in the washer. | Spot‑vac high‑traffic entryway & hallway. | Start the week with a “mini‑launch” – no folding yet. |
| **Tue** | **Wash + fold** – move Monday’s load to dryer, fold while it’s warm; start a second load if needed. | Vacuum living‑room sofa/area rug. | Folding while the dryer runs makes the time feel “free”. |
| **Wed** | **Rest / micro‑catch‑up** – 5 min to toss any stray items (e.g., gym clothes). | Quick‑wipe kitchen floor (just a sweep, not a full pass). | A gentle mid‑week breather keeps the routine from feeling heavy. |
| **Thu** | **Dry & finish** – finish Tuesday’s load, put away folded clothes; start a small “quick‑load” (e.g., socks). | Vacuum bedrooms (just the hallway & under beds). | Keeping bedroom vacuuming short avoids a long haul on the weekend. |
| **Fri** | **Catch‑up load** – any extra items (work‑out gear, weekend laundry). | **Deep‑vac** – 10‑minute full‑house pass (or run a robot if you have one). | Treat Friday as the “weekly deep clean” slot; a set timer prevents it from stretching. |
| **Sat** | **Optional extra** – if a load is still pending, do a quick 5‑minute wash/fold. | Spot‑vac any visible messes that appeared during the day. | No pressure – if everything is already done, skip. |
| **Sun** | **Review & plan** – glance at the weekly checkbox list (see Session 37) and mark ✅ Laundry handled. | **Review** – ✅ Vacuum handled. | Use the **weekly check‑in** template from Session 37 to note any friction, “what felt heavy”, and decide if the point‑person for laundry/vacuum should rotate next week. |

### How to keep it from feeling overwhelming

1. **Use the point‑person model** – each week you’re the “laundry + vacuum point‑person”.  If a busy week hits, the partner with more bandwidth can temporarily step in (per the **flexible chore adjustment** guidance in Session 37).  Rotate the role every 2–4 weeks so it never becomes a permanent load.  
2. **Set a timer** – 5 minutes for spotting, 10 minutes for the deep‑vac. When the timer rings, you stop; the job is “good enough” and you avoid perfectionism.  
3. **Mini‑check‑ins** – The one‑line weekly checkbox list from Session 37 (Laundry handled, Vacuum handled, etc.) gives you a quick visual cue that the work is done, without a big spreadsheet.  
4. **Batch during natural downtime** – Fold clothes while watching a short TV episode or listening to a podcast; vacuum right after the kids leave the room or after dinner dishes are done.  
5. **Fallback rule** – If a work night runs late, the other partner can do a quick “5‑minute tidy” while you take the dishes (the fallback rule from Session 14).  It keeps the system light and drama‑free.

### Quick weekly check‑in script (adapted from Session 37)

> **1. What went smoothly?** – “Laundry stayed on schedule, vacuum felt quick.”  
> **2. Anything felt heavy?** – “Friday deep‑vac took longer than expected.”  
> **3. Adjust?** – “Swap deep‑vac to Saturday next week.”  
> **4. Appreciation?** – “Thanks for covering the extra load on Tuesday.”  

Mark the checklist, note any tweak, and optionally rotate the point‑person.  Over time the schedule becomes a habit, and because each step is bounded by a small time slice, it won’t feel overwhelming.
